newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound regains points against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound regains points against dollar.

text.p: The Lebanese pound regained ground against the dollar in quiet interbank trade in the week ended on Wednesday amid heavy offer of the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The pound closed nearly four points up on the week in interbank trade at 1,544-1,545 to the dollar from 1,548.5 last Friday.
"A big bulk of U.S. dollars came from abroad, creating surplus liquidity in the market and increasing the volume of supply," Byblos Bank Treasurer Shadi Hanna told Reuters.
The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,540-1,548.5 pounds per dollar from 1,540-1,549.5.
"By lowering the offer price by one pound to the dollar this week, the Bank of Lebanon aimed at assuring investors that last week's disturbance did not affect the trend of the maket," Hanna said.
The markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha holiday.
